text:
Neal Pionk is playing 24 minutes a night for a Winnipeg team that has won eight of its last ten games, and he's already past last season's point total: 14 points in 26 games against 12 in 51 a year ago. He's also throwing his body around, with 62 hits.

His points could be higher. The Jets have scored about five fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, the kind of gap that usually closes. His own finishing is fine, four goals on 4.2 expected.

The harder question is defense. Winnipeg is slightly outchanced at five on five on his shifts (about 48% of expected goals), and Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season, with opponents getting more chances when he was out there. Part of that is the job: his competition ranked in the 92nd percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a better note: he exits his own zone with possession 65% of the time. What to watch: whether the Jets keep winning his minutes as the schedule tightens.
headline: Pionk carries the minutes, not the bounces
